bandReport.notes:
Seams clean in both directions. p08 (not mine) ends with Q57 complete, so Q58 starts my band cleanly. p13 (not mine) opens with Q81 under its own 'Consider the following data for the next two (02) items' block, so my last item Q80 completes on p12 and nothing straddles that seam.

DIRECTIONS SET I OWN: the data-sufficiency block 'For the next ten (10) items that follow :' STARTS on p11 (left column, above Q71) and runs Q71-Q80, ending exactly at the foot of p12. All ten members are transcribed here, contiguous, each carrying setLabel 'D71-80' and identical verbatim context. No Directions block starts before p09 that reaches into my pages.

CONVENTION ESTABLISHED (this is the first data-sufficiency block in the cds-maths corpus - grepped 'Statement I' across scripts/cds-maths/data and there are no prior instances): the four (a)-(d) instruction paragraphs printed once inside the Directions block are carried as each item's four OPTIONS, and the 'context' holds only the two-sentence preamble above them. Putting the instruction list in context as well would render it twice on every member, once as stimulus and once as the option list.

An item-specific preamble printed ABOVE its 'Question :' line (Q71, Q75, Q79, Q80) belongs to that item alone, not to the set, so it is the first line of that item's stem rather than context.

No figures on p09-p12. No printed data tables. Decimals printed as raised middle dots (6.72 in Q79, 0.25/0.5/0.75 in Q69, 30.60 m dimensions in Q63) transcribed as full stops per the brief.

questions.stem: The surface area of a cube is increased by 25%. If p is the percentage increase in its length, then which one of the following is correct ?
A solid cube is cut into two cuboids of equal volume. What is the ratio of total surface area of the given cube to that of one of the cuboids ?
The length of a diagonal of a cuboid is 11 cm. The surface area is 240 square cm. What is the sum of its length, breadth and height ?

questions.stem: Let x be the area of a square inscribed in a circle of radius r and y be the area of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the same circle. Which one of the following is correct ?
If the length of a rectangle is increased by \(66\frac{2}{3}\%\), then by what percent should the width of the rectangle be decreased in order to maintain the same area ?
What is the maximum area that can be covered by three non-intersecting circles drawn inside a rectangle of sides 8 cm and 12 cm ?

options.label: A
options.text: \(16\pi\) square cm

options.label: B
options.text: \(18\pi\) square cm

options.label: C
options.text: \(20\pi\) square cm

questions.stem: ABCD is a square field with AB = x. A vertical pole OP of height 2x stands at the centre O of the square field. If \(\angle APO = \theta\), then what is \(\cot\theta\) equal to ?

A solid iron ball is melted and 64 smaller solid balls of equal size are made using the entire volume of iron. What is the ratio of the surface area of the larger ball to the sum of the surface areas of all the smaller balls ?

A triangle ABC has been divided into four smaller triangles P, Q, R, S whose perimeters are 16 cm, 12 cm, 4 cm and 12 cm respectively. P, R and S contain the vertices A, B and C respectively. What is the perimeter of the triangle ABC ?

options.label: A
options.text: 18 cm

options.label: B
options.text: 20 cm

options.label: C
options.text: 22 cm

options.label: D
options.text: 24 cm

flags: No figure is printed with this item on p10 (stem runs straight into the options), yet the stem never states HOW triangle ABC is divided into the four smaller triangles P, Q, R, S. Transcribed exactly as printed - worth a source check that no diagram was dropped in this reprint.
Invented subtopic 'Perimeters of Subdivided Triangles' - no listed Triangles subtopic covers perimeters of sub-triangles; the nearest, 'Ratio of Areas of Triangles', is about areas.
